pages.text: Aegirosaurus leptospondylus is a genus of medium-sized European ichthyosaur. Originally described from the world-famous Jurassic Solnhofen Limestone, it was recently established that the genus survived well into the Cretaceous, into the Valanginian of Southern France, during a notable 13 million years gap in the ichthyosaur fossil record, and therefore surviving largely unscathed the extinction event between the two periods.

Analysis of the teeth and slender snout of French specimens of Aegirosaurus seems to indicate that it was well-adapted to predate on small soft-bodied prey, such as small fish and coleoid cephalopods, like modern bottlenose dolphins.
